title: Indonesia’s Vice President has problems with school papers

paragraphs: Indonesia’s top court has thrown out a case against Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka over his high school credentials.

Gibran is the oldest son of former President Joko Widodo. Critics claimed his high school diploma didn’t meet national requirements for office and wanted to remove him. Under Indonesian election laws, anyone running for vice president must finish high school or must hold a qualification equivalent to it. All nine judges dismissed the case for legal reasons. They said petitioners didn’t have the right to do so because they were not candidates in the 2024 election.

Also, since Gibran has already been sworn in, it is too late to change the election results. However, the judges pointed out that nobody actually showed a graduation certificate to prove his foreign credentials match local standards. So while Gibran remains in power, this issue might cause more trouble for him later on.

paragraphs: The top court in Indonesia dismissed a legal case against Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka. Some people tried to remove him from office and said his school diploma from another country was not high enough for a vice president.

Under Indonesian law, leaders must finish high school or a school equal to it. All nine judges on the court rejected the case for technical legal reasons. They said the people who brought the case were not allowed to do it because they didn’t run in the 2024 election. The judges also said Gibran is already officially in office.
The court noted that nobody showed anything to prove his foreign diploma was valid. For now, Gibran stays in his position, but more legal problems may happen in the future.
